headline: Committee reviews South Maui plan policies, takes testimony, no vote on Bill 108

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: Members heard testimony on the South Maui plan, voted on amendments to several policies, and had a motion on Bill 108-2026 made and seconded with no vote taken. The committee will reconvene on the same Teams link, with in-person viewing in the Council Chambers.
meeting.recap: A testifier said this review process is too rushed.[[0:35:48]] Another testifier said the plan has no financial plan, though the County code requires one.[[1:12:33]] Another testifier said South Maui already has 4,500 approved units, more than the 1,700 needed.[[1:22:20]] The chair held off on an executive session (a closed-door talk with lawyers).[[1:31:22]] The chair said changes to this plan can be made with five votes.[[1:47:34]] A main motion to recommend passing Bill 108 on first reading was made and seconded.[[1:48:37]] Members voted 5–1 to reword a policy so it names affordable and workforce housing projects instead of code sections.[[3:39:49]] The chair said testimony showed fear that Kīhei has no safe, fast way out in emergencies.[[3:42:15]] Members voted 6–0 to call for hālau (gathering) spaces, plural, in South Maui.[[4:26:36]]
decided: A main motion to recommend passage of Bill 108 on first reading was made and seconded; no vote was taken on it today.
A motion to note that policy 2.1.1 ties to actions 1.05A and B was made and seconded; the captions do not record the vote result.
Members voted to tie policy 2.1.2 to actions 1.12 through 1.15 while keeping the word 'implement.'.
Members voted on a blanket motion to tie each policy to its matching implementing actions, with staff to do the work later; the count is unclear in the captions.
A motion to delete policy 2.1.6 and change 2.1.7 so roundabouts must be considered at all new or redesigned intersections was called; the captions cut off before the result.
Members voted to add 'as identified in action 1.02' to policy 2.1.10.
Members voted to add 'to the extent practicable' to a transportation stormwater policy.
meeting.next: The chair said a testifier's cumulative-impact presentation would probably come before Section 4. Members will revisit the mauka bypass policy, which the advisory committee chair said was moved to policy 3.4.5. Staff will follow up with the executive branch on parking passes for the advisory committee resource persons. The committee will reconvene on the same Teams link, with in-person viewing in the Council Chambers.

boards.name: Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

issues.oneLine: Testifiers questioned how many new homes the South Maui plan would allow.
issues.why: A testifier said South Maui already has 4,500 approved units, more than the 1,700 needed.
issues.brief: A testifier said planning research set a maximum of 1,700 homes, but guidance later allowed more than 8,000 units.[[#1]] Another testifier urged the council to reject 3,500 additional housing units proposed in the draft plan.[[#2]] Members voted 5–1 to reword a policy to name affordable and workforce housing projects instead of code sections.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: Members discussed residents' fear that Kīhei lacks a safe, fast way out in emergencies.
issues.why: The chair pointed to the tsunami evacuation, the August 8th, 2023 fires, and frequent mud floods in Kīhei.
issues.brief: A council member asked whether the county could work with the state to map a bypass route early.[[#1]] The council chair said a bypass will take the state, the county, and the community working together.[[#2]]
